title: Your day, in detail
job: Longer habitual narration with sequencing words
verifiedBy: LLM review, authorised by repo owner

allowedPatterns: Je me lève + , + je me lave + et + je m'habille

rules.text: A REFLEXIVE VERB CARRIES ITS OWN LITTLE PRONOUN, AND IT GOES BEFORE THE VERB: je me lave, tu te laves, elle se lave, nous nous lavons, vous vous lavez, ils se lavent. The verb itself is ordinary; only that word in front is new, and it is the same me and te L2-M5 taught as objects. English marks almost none of these — it just says wash, get up, go to bed — so the pronoun is the whole delta.

me, te and se elide to m', t' and s' before a vowel or a silent h: je m'habille, tu t'habilles, elle s'habille. This is obligatory, not a shortcut, and it is written as one word with the apostrophe inside it — the same spelling law as d'habitude and l'après-midi.

A FREQUENCY ADVERB FOLLOWS THE VERB: je bois souvent un café, je vais rarement au cinéma. English puts it in front — I often drink, I rarely go — and a learner who copies that word order writes je souvent bois, which no French speaker says. d'habitude, parfois and chaque matin open the sentence just as happily, because they set the whole clause rather than colour the verb.

jamais NEEDS ITS ne: je ne mange jamais. jamais is not a negative word on its own — the pair ne … jamais is, exactly as ne … pas is. Speech drops the ne and you will hear je mange jamais, but writing it that way produces something no French text contains, so write both halves every time.

The sequencing spine is already yours — d'abord, ensuite (L2-M10), puis (L1-M10), enfin — and a whole day runs in the present with nothing else added. The passé composé tells what happened yesterday; the present tells what happens every day, however long the account gets.

sentences.display: D'habitude je me lève à sept heures
sentences.cue: I usually get up at seven
sentences.literal: Of habit I me raise at seven hours

words.note: One key with its apostrophe inside: de + habitude. It opens the sentence and sets the whole account as a habit. The bare habitude is a noun you do not need here.

sentences.trap: me lève is not I lift myself. French marks the verb with a pronoun where English changes verb altogether — rise becomes get up — and the me carries no stress and never translates.
sentences.sound: da-bee-TÜD zhuh muh LEHV a set UR. The d' and habitude run together as one word and the h is silent.

variations.display: D'habitude je me lève tard
variations.cue: I usually get up late

variations.display: Je me lève à sept heures
variations.cue: I get up at seven

mistake.display: D'habitude je lève à sept heures
mistake.why: lever without the pronoun means lifting something else. Your own getting up needs me: D'habitude je me lève à sept heures.

sentences.usage: The opening line of any account of your day.
sentences.mnemonic: d'habitude opens the day; the me stays glued in front of the verb.

sentences.display: Je me réveille tôt mais je me lève tard
sentences.cue: I wake up early but I get up late
sentences.literal: I me wake early but I me raise late

words.note: Waking and getting up are two verbs in French too: je me réveille is the eyes opening, je me lève is the feet on the floor.
The opposite of L2-M10's tard, and just as free: it goes where tard goes. Final t silent — toh.

sentences.trap: réveiller somebody and lever somebody are things you do TO them. Both need the pronoun before they say anything about you, and the pair is not interchangeable in French any more than in English.
sentences.sound: zhuh muh ray-VEY toh meh zhuh muh LEHV tar. The final t of tôt and the d of tard are both silent.

variations.display: Je me réveille tôt et je travaille
variations.cue: I wake up early and I work

variations.display: Ma sœur se réveille tard
variations.cue: My sister wakes up late
variations.changed: a different person, so me becomes se

mistake.display: Je réveille tôt mais je me lève tard
mistake.why: réveiller on its own wakes somebody else up. Waking yourself needs the pronoun: Je me réveille tôt.

sentences.usage: The honest version of your morning, when the two do not happen together.
sentences.mnemonic: réveille is the eyes, lève is the feet.

sentences.display: D'abord je me lave, ensuite je m'habille
sentences.cue: First I wash, then I get dressed
sentences.literal: First I me wash, next I me-dress

words.note: laver is to wash something; me lave washes ME. The pronoun changes with the person and never moves: tu te laves, elle se lave.
me + habille, written as one elided key. The h of habiller is silent, so me must become m' — je me habille is not a slower way of saying it.

sentences.trap: The elision is obligatory. A silent h counts as a vowel for every rule French has, so habiller behaves exactly like a word starting with a.
sentences.sound: da-BOR zhuh muh LAHV, ahn-SWEET zhuh ma-BEEY. The h of m'habille is silent and the ill is a y.

variations.display: D'abord je me lave, puis je m'habille
variations.cue: First I wash, then I get dressed

variations.display: Je me lave et je m'habille
variations.cue: I wash and I get dressed

mistake.display: D'abord je me lave, ensuite je me habille
mistake.why: The h of habiller is silent, so the pronoun elides: ensuite je m'habille.

sentences.usage: Two steps of a morning in one line, which is what the sequencing words are for.
sentences.mnemonic: Before a vowel the pronoun loses its own vowel.

sentences.display: Le matin je bois souvent un café
sentences.cue: In the morning I often drink a coffee
sentences.literal: The morning I drink often a coffee

words.note: It goes AFTER the verb — je bois souvent — where English puts often in front of it. Final t silent: soo-VAHN.

sentences.trap: je souvent bois is the word order English hands a learner, and it is the one order French will not take. The adverb waits until the verb has been said.
sentences.sound: luh ma-TAN zhuh bwa soo-VAHN un ka-FAY. The en of souvent is the nasal of dans.

variations.display: Le soir je bois souvent un thé
variations.cue: In the evening I often drink a tea

variations.display: Je bois souvent de l'eau
variations.cue: I often drink water

mistake.display: Le matin je souvent bois un café
mistake.why: The frequency word follows the verb: Le matin je bois souvent un café.

sentences.usage: Describing what usually, but not always, happens.

sentences.display: Je ne mange jamais le matin
sentences.cue: I never eat in the morning
sentences.literal: I not eat never the morning

words.note: It needs the ne in front of the verb: je NE mange JAMAIS. jamais alone is not a negative word — the pair is, exactly like ne … pas.

sentences.trap: Speech drops the ne and you will hear je mange jamais all day long. Write it that way and you have produced something no French text contains, so the written half stays.
sentences.sound: zhuh nuh mahnzh zha-MEH luh ma-TAN. The s of jamais is silent.

variations.display: Je ne mange jamais le soir
variations.cue: I never eat in the evening

variations.display: Je ne bois jamais de café le matin
variations.cue: I never drink coffee in the morning
variations.changed: a drink, where the negative turns du into de

mistake.why: jamais keeps its ne however speech treats it: Je ne mange jamais le matin.

sentences.usage: Stating a habit you do not have.
sentences.mnemonic: ne … jamais is one word split around the verb.

sentences.display: L'après-midi je me repose à la maison
sentences.cue: In the afternoon I rest at home
sentences.literal: The-afternoon I me rest at the house

words.note: One key with its elision inside: le + après-midi. As a time expression it stands alone, with no preposition in front of it at all.
Same shape as me lave: reposer rests something, me repose rests ME. tu te reposes, il se repose.

sentences.trap: English says in the afternoon and French says the afternoon. l'après-midi carries the time by itself, exactly as le matin and le soir do, and en l'après-midi is not French at all.
sentences.sound: la-preh-mee-DEE zhuh muh ruh-POHZ a la meh-ZON. The s of après is silent.

variations.display: Le soir je me repose à la maison
variations.cue: In the evening I rest at home
variations.changed: a different part of the day

variations.display: L'après-midi je ne travaille pas
variations.cue: In the afternoon I don't work

mistake.display: En l'après-midi je me repose à la maison
mistake.why: The time expression needs no preposition in front of it: L'après-midi je me repose à la maison.

sentences.usage: The middle of a day, between the morning and the evening.
sentences.mnemonic: l'après-midi is already in the afternoon.

sentences.display: Parfois je mange une pomme le soir
sentences.cue: Sometimes I eat an apple in the evening
sentences.literal: Sometimes I eat an apple the evening

words.note: One of the two frequency words free to open a sentence — Parfois je mange — or to follow the verb — je mange parfois. Both are ordinary.

sentences.trap: parfois moves freely — in front of the clause or after the verb, with nothing else changing. souvent and rarement stay after the verb in ordinary speech, and jamais never goes anywhere without its ne.
sentences.sound: par-FWA zhuh mahnzh ün pom luh SWAR. The oi is wa and the final s is silent.

variations.display: Je mange parfois une pomme le soir
variations.cue: I sometimes eat an apple in the evening
variations.changed: parfois after the verb instead of in front

variations.display: Parfois je bois du thé le soir
variations.cue: Sometimes I drink tea in the evening

mistake.display: Parfois je mange un pomme le soir
mistake.why: pomme is feminine and L1-M3 taught it so: Parfois je mange une pomme le soir.

sentences.usage: An occasional habit, said without committing to it.
sentences.mnemonic: parfois may lead; souvent may not.

sentences.cue: I rarely go to the cinema

words.note: French builds adverbs the way English builds -ly: rare + ment. It sits after the verb, exactly like souvent — je vais rarement.

sentences.trap: rarement is a plain negative-ish word and takes no ne. Only jamais drags the ne along with it, which is why it is the one that trips people.
sentences.sound: zhuh veh rar-MAHN o see-nay-MA. The e of rarement is swallowed: rar-MAHN.

variations.display: Je vais rarement au marché
variations.cue: I rarely go to the market

variations.display: Je vais souvent au cinéma
variations.cue: I often go to the cinema

mistake.why: The adverb waits for the verb: Je vais rarement au cinéma.

sentences.usage: Saying something happens, but hardly ever.

sentences.display: Je me couche toujours à dix heures
sentences.cue: I always go to bed at ten
sentences.literal: I me lay always at ten hours

words.note: The whole person set on one verb: je me couche, tu te couches, elle se couche, nous nous couchons, vous vous couchez, ils se couchent.

sentences.trap: coucher somebody is what you do to a child at bedtime. The pronoun is the only thing that turns it into your own going to bed, and dropping it changes who is put to bed.
sentences.sound: zhuh muh KOOSH too-ZHOOR a deez UR. The x of dix links onto heures as a z.

variations.display: Ma sœur se couche tard
variations.cue: My sister goes to bed late
variations.changed: a different person, so me becomes se

variations.display: Tu te couches à dix heures ?
variations.cue: Do you go to bed at ten?
variations.changed: a question to somebody you know well, so me becomes te

mistake.display: Je couche toujours à dix heures
mistake.why: Without me it says you put somebody else to bed: Je me couche toujours à dix heures.

sentences.usage: The last line of the day, and the one a host asks about.
sentences.mnemonic: No pronoun, no bed of your own.

sentences.display: Chaque matin je bois un thé
sentences.cue: Every morning I drink a tea
sentences.literal: Each morning I drink a tea

words.note: chaque takes a SINGULAR noun, always: chaque matin, never chaque matins. L1-M4's tous les jours says the same thing with a plural.

sentences.trap: English every takes a singular and all takes a plural, and French splits them the same way. What English does not do is offer two everyday idioms for one daily habit — chaque matin and tous les matins are both ordinary.
sentences.sound: shak ma-TAN zhuh bwa un TAY. chaque is one syllable, shak.

variations.display: Tous les jours je bois un thé
variations.cue: Every day I drink a tea
variations.changed: tous les jours instead of chaque matin

variations.display: Chaque matin je bois un café
variations.cue: Every morning I drink a coffee

mistake.display: Chaque matins je bois un thé
mistake.why: chaque is followed by a singular: Chaque matin je bois un thé.

sentences.usage: Closing an account of your day with the thing that never changes.
sentences.mnemonic: chaque counts one at a time.
